research_review.summary: Slater is the safest listed £4.5m replacement: he has started all three matches, played 270 minutes and retains some corner involvement. Predicted-lineup sources also expect him to start, whereas Hughes has a less secure outlook. However, Hull visit Chelsea in GW4 and then Newcastle, so the engine's claimed 20.6-point five-week gain looks greatly overstated; independent projections put Slater near 2–3 points per match. No chip is justified: the Bench Boost bench is weak, while using Triple Captain, Free Hit or Wildcard this early would sacrifice flexibility before the first chip set expires after GW19. Treat all GW5–GW18 transfers and chip targets as provisional rather than commitments.
